response.justification: The candidate is a highly experienced, versatile software engineer with strong distributed-systems and Linux backgrounds, plus notable geospatial/GIS side-project experience, but his core professional stack is JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, and DLang rather than modern C++ or Rust, which are the primary required technologies for this role. His most recent hands-on C/C++ work dates back to 2014-2015, making him a weak match for a role centered on performance-critical routing tile pipelines in C++.
strengths: Extensive distributed-systems and microservices experience (e.g., Sociomantic/Dunnhumby handling millions of requests/sec)
Direct geospatial/GIS domain experience through GISCollective and Green Map projects
Demonstrated adaptability across many languages and stacks over a long career, showing willingness to learn new areas
concerns: Little recent professional C++ experience (last significant C/C++ work was 2014-2015 at National Instruments)
No Rust experience mentioned at all
Primary recent focus is full-stack TypeScript/Node.js work, not systems-level or performance-critical backend engineering

key_factors.factor: Lack of recent C++/Rust production experience
Strong distributed systems and low-latency service experience (though in DLang/Node)
